title: NGS-based analysis of the mouse B-cell receptor repertoire
protocol: Obtain nucleotide sequences of the mouse IGHV and IGHJ regions from the IMGT genome database.
Perform sequence alignment for each gene segment (IGHV and IGHJ).
Create a frequency plot using WebLogo for aligned sequences.
Design primer sequences based on single base frequencies within aligned sequences.
Generate two different degenerated forward primers for the IGHV gene segment framework region 1 (FR1) clusters.
Generate one degenerated reverse primer for the IGHJ gene segment.
Determine gDNA concentration of CD5+/CD19+ sorted CLL cells using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Use 30 ng of gDNA as a template for PCR amplification.
Dilute primer stocks \(100 µM) of RG1269, RG1270, and RG1271 to a final concentration of 10 µM using nuclease-free water.
Mix equal volumes of each diluted primer to generate a primer mix with 10 µM of each primer.
Set up the first PCR reaction in 0.2 ml PCR tubes.
Start PCR reaction using the following cycler program.
Take AMPure XP beads out of the fridge and allow them to reach room temperature.
Vortex AMPure XP beads for 30 seconds to ensure homogeneity.
Bring 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.5) solution to room temperature.
Prepare 80% ethanol solution freshly at room temperature.
Add 20 µl AMPure XP beads to each PCR reaction and mix well by pipetting up and down until beads are resuspended.
Incubate the mixture for 5 min at room temperature.
Place the samples on a magnetic stand (e.g., DynaMag-96 Side Magnet) and wait until the beads form a pellet and the supernatant is clear.
Remove the supernatant without destroying the bead pellet.
Keep samples on the magnetic stand while washing twice with 200 µl 80% ethanol solution.
Incubate for 30 seconds after adding each wash of ethanol before removing it.
Make sure to remove all remaining ethanol after each wash step.
Incubate on room temperature for 10 min until residual ethanol is evaporated, but do not over dry the bead pellet.
Resuspend the dry bead pellet in 52.5 μl 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.5) until the solution is homogenous.
Incubate the mixture for 5 min at room temperature.
Place the samples back on the magnetic stand and wait until the beads form a pellet and the supernatant is clear.
Transfer 50 μl of the supernatant into a new PCR tube without destroying the bead pellet.
Dilute primer stocks RG1272, RG1273, and RG1274 together to a final concentration of 1 µM.
Mix 10 μl of each 100 µM primer stock with 970 μl of nuclease-free water in one tube.
Set up the second PCR reaction according to Table 4 (components for 2nd PCR reaction).
Start the PCR reaction using the cycler program detailed in Table 5.
Repeat steps from 9 to 20 to purify the PCR product of the second PCR reaction.
Store reactions at -15°C to -25°C for up to one week if necessary.
Analyze samples on a D1000 ScreenTape in a TapeStation system to monitor successful amplification and removal of residual primers.
Determine the peak molarity [nmol/l] of the PCR product by integrating under the peak.
Calculate the volume inserted for the indexing PCR based on the peak molarity.
Set up indexing PCR reaction in 0.2 ml PCR tubes as specified.
Start PCR reaction using the cycler program provided.
Purify the indexing PCR reaction.
Repeat step 9 to 20 to purify the PCR product with minor modifications.
Use 27.5 µl of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.5) for resuspension of the beads.
Transfer 25 µl of the supernatant into a new DNA LoBind Tube without disturbing the bead pellet.
Analyze 1:10 to 1:50 diluted samples in a D1000 ScreenTape on a TapeStation system using 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.5.
Monitor successful amplification and removal of residual primers with a PCR product length around 520 bp.
Check if the main peak is above 90% of the integrated area without impurities.
Determine the DNA concentration [ng/µl] of the purified PCR product using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Calculate the DNA concentration in nM as follows: \[Equation 1\].
Dilute each sample to a final concentration of 4 nM in 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.5) in DNA LoBind Tubes.
Pool equimolar amounts, e.g., 5 µl per sample in a DNA LoBind Tube.
Determine the DNA concentration [ng/µl] of the library pool using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Combine 5 µl of the 4 nM library pool with 5 µl of 0.2 N NaOH (freshly prepared) in a DNA LoBind Tube.
Mix by vortexing and spin down the combined solution.
Incubate the combined solution at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 990 µl pre-chilled HT1 buffer to obtain a 20 pM denatured library.
Keep the library on ice.
Dilute the denatured library to 8 pM by combining 240 µl of the 20 pM denatured library with 360 µl pre-chilled HT1 buffer.
Keep the diluted and denatured library on ice until sequencing.
Prepare the MiSeqDx system for a sequencing run according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Use the Illumina Experiment Manager Software in FASTQ only Run Settings to generate the sample sheet.
Sequence with the MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600-cycle).
For bioinformatic analysis, use MiXCR software v2.1.8 and the reference library repseqio.v1.4.
Change the species parameter setting to Mus musculus.
